title: Latency Orchestrator: cohort-based dashboard with streaming vs non-streaming splits
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a production-grade dashboard that surfaces per-model and per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) with an explicit split for streaming vs non-streaming I/O modes, plus cohort slices (request token length, conversation turns, concurrency bucket, quantization profile). This ticket covers design + infra plumbing: tracing hook tagging, metrics pipeline enrichment, and dashboard panels with drilldowns to traces and error logs.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: telemetry schema changes to add 'io_mode', 'quant_profile', 'request_token_bins'; tracing hook updates to propagate io_mode and model_variant; metrics transformation in the pipeline (Prometheus -> OTLP enrichment -> metrics datastore); 3 dashboard panels (overview heatmap, percentile timeseries per model/route, cohort waterfall) and links to traces/Logs for the top tail.
- Out of scope: automated SLO bucketing or alerting (follow-on ticket), on-prem telemetry agent work.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Backend: spans and request metrics include stable tags: io_mode=(streaming|nonstreaming), model_route, model_variant, quant_profile, request_token_bucket, concurrency_bucket.
2) Metrics pipeline: new enrichment step injects cohort labels and computes p50/p95/p99 rolling windows by model_route x io_mode.
3) Dashboards: three new panels under Observability -> Latency: (a) model-route percentile matrix with streaming/nonstreaming columns, (b) timeseries explorer with toggle for percentiles and I/O mode, (c) cohort waterfall showing tail contributors and top trace links.
4) Drilldown: clicking a cell links to sampled traces filtered by same cohort tags and to the error log query for that cohort.
5) Performance: metric ingestion cost increase under 8% for the extra labels (validated in staging).
6) Tests: e2e test validates tags appear on spans and metrics during synthetic workload.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Prefer tagging io_mode at the request boundary rather than after response emission to ensure consistent metrics for streaming requests. This requires the trace hook to be available in the streaming response path and to attach io_mode preemptively.
- We will avoid high-cardinality by bucketing request_token_bins (e.g., <32, 32-128, 128-512, 512+), and limiting quant_profile to enumerated labels (fp16/int8/q4_0/q4_1).
- Sampling: keep current trace sampling rates but add deterministic sampling for high-tail cohorts to ensure tail traces are captured. This is a temporary increase in sampled traces for specific cohorts.
- Metrics datastore queries will pre-aggregate percentiles using t-digest windows to reduce query cost while preserving accuracy for p95/p99.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1: tracing hook changes + unit tests (ENG), schema PR for metrics enrichment (infra).
- Week 2: metrics pipeline rollout in staging, dashboard panels prototype (observability).
- Week 3: validation under synthetic workloads, cost check, PR reviews, and merge.
- Week 4: canary in prod for a small set of models/routes, gather feedback, and iterate.
